correctness.rationale: Pinned RESULT.md defines all-symbol availability (2,2,2) using two disjoint helper sets of size <=2 per coordinate, each punctured local linear code having distance >=2. An independent enumeration traversed all C(15,7)=6435 length-8 binary rank-three column-multiplicity profiles including possible zero columns, evaluated all seven nonzero messages for d>=4, and directly checked each size-1/2 helper set via punctured codeword weights. Exactly 28 survive. All 168 GL(3,2) maps split survivors into orbits 21 and 7, represented by A=(1,1,2,2,4,5,6,7) and B=(1,1,2,3,4,5,6,7). Recomputed weight enumerators 1+5z^4+2z^6 and 1+3z^4+4z^5, and 2D-support profiles 6:2,7:4,8:1 and 6:1,7:6. GL stabilizers 8 and 24 and internal equal-column permutations 4 and 2 yield automorphism orders 32 and 48. The classification is exclusively linear size-eight [8,3,4] codes, not arbitrary nonlinear equality cases. Source nonlinear maximum 8 is cited, not independently reestablished here.

originality.rationale: The paper establishing the new nonlinear optimum supplies one attaining binary construction, whereas this work classifies two permutation-inequivalent dimension-three linear attaining classes under the precise all-symbol availability constraint. A generic binary [8,3,4] classification or simplex/Hadamard code does not by itself establish availability of two disjoint local repair sets. Focused published-result searches showed only different LRC parameters. The full recent primary manuscript was not accessible for a page-level comparison, so an appendix equality characterization remains a real residual originality risk.

value.rationale: A natural equality-classification problem for the first newly exact binary availability-two parameter row, where the published nonlinear bound is sharp and the exhibited code is not uniquely forced within linear codes. Identifying precisely two inequivalent extremizers, their distance/support spectra, and automorphism symmetries gives a concrete benchmark for finite LRC design. It is a complete motivated finite invariant, not an arbitrary slice; does not claim asymptotic methods.

limitations: Only binary linear dimension 3 size 8 extremizers; no nonlinear extremizer classification.
